Moreover, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva great being practices the six perfections and sees beings born in the four modes of birth — those born from eggs, those born from a womb, those born from warmth and moisture, and those born miraculously — he should reflect thus: "May it be that in the buddha-field where I fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, the three modes of birth — from eggs, from a womb, and from warmth and moisture — do not occur and do not exist, and that instead all beings are born miraculously." In such a way he should practice the six perfections. "I shall purify the buddha-field. I shall bring beings to maturity." Thus he should reflect. Subhūti, a bodhisattva great being who practices in this way fully completes the six perfections and also comes near to omniscience.
